newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones index sets another new record.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones index sets another new record.

text.p: A strong quarterly profit report from Eastman Kodak Co. Thursday propelled the blue-chip Dow Jones index to a new high despite an inflation scare that rattled investors' nerves.

The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 38.49 points at 6,765.37, which edged out Tuesday's record of 6,762.29. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,330 to 1,185 on heavy volume of 532 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks and NYSE Composite index also set new highs.

The market clawed its way back into the plus column following a selloff that erased a gain of 55 points in the Dow on Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer's comments that he saw a risk of higher inflation.
"There's a lot of volatility," said Bob Dickey, Dain Bosworth technical analyst.
Both the stock and bond markets have been on edge, reacting to any news or economic data that might tip the Fed toward raising interest rates.

"This market has got a bit of a case of nerves," said Michael LaTronica, director of research at Gruntal. "But that's a symptom of a market that has come as far as this one has in the last couple of years."
Kodak, the top gainer in the 30-stock index, rose 4-1/4 to 85-1/2 after its earnings beat Wall Street expectations and it raised its quarterly dividend.

The Nasdaq Composite index closed up 6.93 points at 1,340.46, buoyed by earnings news from Sun Microsystems Inc., which rose 2-13/16 to 31-1/16. Late Wednesday it reported a 41-percent leap in earnings and record revenues for the latest quarter.
But while stocks recovered, bonds stayed weak.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond lost 14/32, raising its yield to 6.83 percent from 6.79 percent at Wednesday's close. The bond's price moves in the opposite direction of its yield.
Analysts said they expected more whipsaw action as stocks try to absorb institutional investor cash flows, corporate earnings news and continued inflation concerns.
"It's just a real split market because of all the different cross currents that are occurring right now," Dickey said.
Digital Equipment Corp. rose 2-1/2 to 36-3/4 after the company's quarterly earnings topped analysts' estimates.
General Electric Co. posted fourth-quarter profits that matched analysts' estimates and its stock ended off 1-3/8 at 101-1/2.
Drug giant Pfizer Inc.'s quarterly results also matched Wall Street expectations and the company said it expects double-digit growth in sales and profits in 1997. The stock rose 3/8 to 87-1/4.

Value Health Inc., a provider of speciality health-care services, rose 1-3/4 to 22 after its merger with Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp., the nation's largest for-profit provider of health care services. Columbia/HCA ended off one at 39-1/4.
Apple Computer Inc. dropped 1/2 to 16-3/4 after the computer maker reported a loss for the latest quarter and warned that it did not expect to report a profit until September.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 2.55 points to 769.75, a new high. The American Stock Exchange index was up 0.88 to 587.36.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 1.08 to 406.12, a new high. The average share was up 12 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 7,447.648, up 21.182, or 0.29 percent.
